newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hijos de J Barreras SA wins order to make NZ ferry.
newsitem.headline: Hijos de J Barreras SA wins order to make NZ ferry.

text.p: New Zealand railroad and inter-island ferry operator Tranz Rail Ltd said on Tuesday it had chosen Spanish company Hijos de J Barreras SA of the Astileros Espanoles Group to build it a new ferry.
No price was disclosed but Tranz Rail said it was spending NZ$500 million to replace its ferries and terminal over 11 years.
Media estimates put the cost of the ferry at NZ$80-100 million.
The new ferry will replace the Aratika. Tranz Rail estimated the replacement cost of that, plus the purchase price of a smaller fast ferry, would be NZ$150 million.
The new ship, 150 metres long and able to carry 350 passengers, is expected to be operating for the 1998/99 summer season.
The ferry will be used until the commissioning of two much bigger ferries when the company gets approval for a new South Island ferry terminal at Clifford Bay, south of Blenheim.
Tranz Rail managing director Francis Small said the company chose the Spanish shipyard because of its extensive experience in building similar vessels.
"We were impressed by the co-operation and innovation of the Spanish and are confident they will build us an excellent vessel that will conform to the highest international safety rules."
The ferry would be built in the company's Vigo shipyard about 30 km north of the Portuguese border on the Spanish northwest coast.

Features on the ship included internal ramps between the rail and vehicle decks. It would be able to operate in a variety of wharf configurations with the addition of a side-loading door as well as the traditional double link spans.
